why: I checked each verifier check's PASS/FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1's expect line is "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case". That fixes the order: flag first, then name. Its PASS condition also requires `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` to work, and its FAIL condition triggers if "either command exits non-zero". The reversed order and the exit-code test are stricter than the words. They belong under Advisory. Check 2 ("without --shout the output is unchanged") also compares exit codes between head and base. An exit code is not output, so this goes further than the words. Checks 3 and 4 stay within their expect lines, and the Advisory section is used correctly for the other extras. Check 1 breaks the criterion, so it does not hold for the whole output.
